# 🚀 Space Flight Briefing: Metal Reactivity Series & Gas Traps

Welcome to the **Orbital Chemical Laboratory**, Astronaut Keithley! In this mission, we navigate the electrochemical activity series of planetary metals.

### 1. Planetary Reactivity Ranking
$$\text{K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > (H) > Cu > Ag > Au}$$
- **Metals standing before $(H)$:** React with dilute acids ($\text{HCl}, \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) to liberate hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2\uparrow$):
  $$\text{Fe} + 2\text{HCl} \to \text{FeCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\uparrow$$
- **Metals standing after $(H)$:** Completely inert in dilute non-oxidizing acids ($\text{Cu}, \text{Ag}, \text{Au}$ do not react).

### 2. Insoluble Residue Principle
When treating an alloy of $\text{Fe}$ and $\text{Cu}$ with excess $\text{HCl}$, only $\text{Fe}$ dissolves into aqueous solution. The unreacted $\text{Cu}$ precipitates as solid insoluble residue:
$$m_{\text{residue}} = m_{\text{Cu}} \implies m_{\text{Fe}} = m_{\text{alloy}} - m_{\text{Cu}}$$

questions.content_markdown: When dropping an asteroidal powder alloy composed of iron ($\text{Fe}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) into excess dilute hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$), which substance undergoes a chemical reaction?

options.text: Both $\text{Fe}$ and $\text{Cu}$ react simultaneously with the acid.
Neither substance reacts with the acid solution.

questions.explanation: ANSWER B: Iron stands before Hydrogen in the reactivity series and reacts vigorously: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2↑. Copper stands after Hydrogen and remains inert.

questions.sectionName: Sector 1: Mercury Orbit • Selective Gas Trap
questions.content_markdown: A planetary ore canister has a total mass of $20.0\text{ g}$ containing zinc ($\text{Zn}$) and silver ($\text{Ag}$). Sensor telemetry determines that the mass of silver ($\text{Ag}$) is $5.0\text{ g}$. What is the **mass percentage** of zinc ($\text{Zn}$) in the canister?

questions.sectionName: Sector 3: Earth Mission Control • Numerical Telemetry
questions.content_markdown: An alloy sample weighing $10.0\text{ g}$ containing magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) is reacted with excess dilute sulfuric acid. After complete reaction, $4.0\text{ g}$ of insoluble copper residue remains. Calculate the mass of magnesium in grams. (Enter numerical value only):
questions.explanation: ANSWER: 6 g. Copper does not react: m(Cu) = 4.0 g. Therefore, m(Mg) = 10.0 - 4.0 = 6.0 g.

questions.sectionName: Sector 7: Uranus Deep Space • Stoichiometric Telemetry
questions.content_markdown: Explain step-by-step how to separate and calculate the individual masses of iron ($\text{Fe}$) and copper ($\text{Cu}$) from a solid mixture using dilute hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$) and filtration. Write the balanced chemical equation.
questions.rubric: 1) Add excess dilute HCl to dissolve Fe. 2) Write Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2↑. 3) Filter insoluble Cu, wash, dry, and weigh. 4) Calculate m(Fe) = m(mixture) - m(Cu).
questions.explanation:
MODEL SOLUTION:
1. Treat mixture with excess dilute HCl: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2↑.
2. Cu is inert in dilute HCl and remains solid.
3. Filter out solid Cu, wash with distilled water, dry, and record m(Cu).
4. Deduce m(Fe) = m(mixture) - m(Cu).
